```json
{
  "tests": [
    {
      "name": "Happy path with one argument",
      "given": "args = []string{\"NAME\"}",
      "expect": "nil",
      "polarity": "success",
      "covers": "happy"
    },
    {
      "name": "Empty input is allowed",
      "given": "args = []string{}",
      "expect": "nil",
      "polarity": "success",
      "covers": "happy"
    },
    {
      "name": "More than one argument",
      "given": "args = []string{\"NAME\", \"EXTRA\"}",
      "expect": "error: argument count is invalid",
      "polarity": "negative",
      "covers": "error:1"
    }
  ]
}
```

```go
package cli

import (
	"testing"
)

func TestValidateArgs(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		args    []string
		wantErr bool
	}{
		{
			name:    "Happy path with one argument",
			args:    []string{"NAME"},
			wantErr: false,
		},
		{
			name:    "Empty input is allowed",
			args:    []string{},
			wantErr: false,
		},
		{
			name:    "More than one argument",
			args:    []string{"NAME", "EXTRA"},
			wantErr: true,
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			err := validateArgs(tt.args)
			if (err != nil) != tt.wantErr {
				t.Errorf("validateArgs() error = %v, wantErr %v", err, tt.wantErr)
			}
		})
	}
}
```
